answer: Mutual-consumption ledger. Each identity must route real work through a sparrow-tagged counterparty, and payouts clear only when both sides log matching consumption within a window, so fake clusters must simulate genuine bidirectional demand. The garden of accounts an attacker spins up cannot just self-deal: every fabricated edge requires funding a second synthetic consumer and eating the spread on each cleared trade. A vine of coordinated fakes collapses when the per-pair loss exceeds the reward, making each identity cost real value rather than a one-time registration.
